title.narrative: UNODC PSF Project on Strengthening PK's response to spreading of violent extremism virtually & among youths

description.narrative: Background and project description Over the past 15 years, Pakistan has faced significant challenges from terrorism and extremism, which have not only threatened national security and social cohesion but also violated the human rights of its most vulnerable citizens. While the Pakistani government has made progress in reducing the threat from terrorist hideouts, there is growing concern about the crime-terror relationship in urban areas, an increase in terror attacks on law enforcement agencies, and a new wave of terrorist recruitment. The recent takeover of Afghanistan by the Taliban has further complicated the security situation in both Afghanistan and Pakistan, potentially leading to increased instability and emboldening of terrorist and subnationalist groups. These groups exploit vulnerable individuals online for recruitment, inciting violence, and radicalization. To address these issues, the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) is working with its donor partners to provide technical assistance to the Pakistani government in effectively preventing violent extremism through the strengthening of its criminal justice response. Pakistan has implemented the National Action Plan (NAP) and National Counter Extremism Policy Guidelines to prevent threats arising from violent extremism that can evolve into terrorism. The National Counter Terrorism Authority (NACTA) has been revitalized to take the lead in coordinating efforts with all provinces. Since 2017, UNODC has collaborated closely with the Pakistani government through the project known as 'Pakistan's Action to Counter Terrorism - PACT'. This project aimed to contribute to the fight against terrorism, particularly in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) and Sindh provinces, by improving criminal justice processes. PACT has achieved significant success, gaining strong support from government counterparts and enhancing the investigative capabilities and use of forensic evidence by the KP and Sindh police. The project

The objective of the development cooperation is (i) to increase the capacity and capability of Pakistan’s enforcement bodies to prevent violent extremism (especially online), (ii) to increase interagency coordination on implementing PVE strategies, and (iii) to ultimately improve the rule of law in Pakistan and bolster regional stability. To achieve these goals, the project will be implemented under UNODC’s Country Programme III (2022-2025).
The Danish Mission of Islamabad will base the actual support on progress attained in the implementation of the project as described in the documentation provided by the Grantee or in this jointly agreed document. Progress will be measured through the UNODC’s monitoring framework.
